what: A usage error's try: line, printed as the corrected command, was a command the tool refused. speedramp.py IN --ramp 3:6:0.5 -o OUT suggested --segment 3:6:0.5 (speedramp takes START-END:FACTOR): --segment was the one option whose help mentions 'ramp', and the value written for --ramp went with it. A sweep of every rule over tests/sweep.py's table printed 1069 distinct try: lines and 533 of them were refused; the 466 that were not the caller's own value or context (457 from a flag the tool lacks, 9 from a choice) had three causes: an option that only mentions the word or shares a word with the flag (audio.py --preset ultrafast became --voice ultrafast, --strength low became --denoise-strength low), an option spelt like a flag another tool takes (pad.py --smart became --start with no value, export.py --alpha-codec png became --alpha-mode png, check.py --top 1 became --tp 1), and a common other word mapped past the choices (check.py --platform strong became ig, the platform nearest to 'high'; graphics.py --template mid became meme).
escaped: test_a_mistake_with_one_answer_is_followed_by_the_corrected_command ran the three commands its own cases print, all spelling mistakes of the tool's own options, and docs/design-decisions.md said 'the command is one the tool takes, and the test runs each'. Nothing ran the commands a flag another tool takes, or a word only a help text uses, would print, which is what a caller who guesses writes.
mechanism: runner._teach answers a flag only with one option spelt like it (difflib 0.85) and only when no tool, in its own file or a shared module, declares the flag; a common other word is the answer only when it is one of the choices. tests/test_contract.py's StumbleLedgerTests.test_a_try_line_is_a_command_the_tool_accepts runs every rule (a misspelt option with its value, a misspelt choice and every common other word, a number with its unit) on every tool of tests/sweep.py's table but verify.py, asserts that no option of another tool is answered with a command, and runs each printed command with --dry-run; it also pins speedramp --ramp. docs/design-decisions.md ('try: is printed only when it is known') now says what the command corrects and what it does not.
